# Step-preserving maps transport finite traces

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`finite-trace-transport` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](finite-trace-transport.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> A map preserving each step of one process into another sends every finite course to a course with the same moves; the converse, endpoints included, holds exactly where every step from an image lifts from each configuration with that image.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Where a map f takes every step of P to a step of Q by the same move, every finite trace of P from s to t is a trace of Q from f s to f t with the same moves. (`Generative.trace_map`)
2. Where, for every s, every step of Q from q s lifts to a step of P from s by the same move into the fiber of its target, every trace of Q from q s to r is the image of a trace of P from s whose end lies in the fiber of r. (`Generative.trace_lift`)
3. Through a map q, the traces of Q from q s are exactly the images of the traces of P from s, endpoints included, for every s, exactly where q preserves every step and every step of Q from q s lifts to a step of P from s by the same move into the fiber of its target. (`Generative.projection_exact_iff`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- Two supplied processes on configurations of any kind, with one type of moves; transport takes step preservation (hstep) as its hypothesis, lifting takes the lifting condition (hlift), and the exactness law states both as the condition of its equivalence.
- Traces are finite: a list of moves with every intermediate configuration carried.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- Step preservation alone does not give the converse: lifting needs a condition at every configuration of each starting fiber. Witness: `Generative.projection_exact_iff`.

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used.
